datasetMetadata.title: Cloud & Sensor-Dropout Exclusion (Synthetic)
datasetMetadata.description: Synthetic 24×24 image pair demonstrating per-date cloud validity masks (42 masked pixels in before, 35 in after) and 2 zero-denominator pixels (79 total invalid pixels, 497 eligible pixels) alongside a 36-pixel changed zone.

summaryStatistics.percentageDenominatorDescription: Change percentages (candidateChangedPercentage and retainedChangedPercentage) use eligiblePixelCount (pixels valid with finite NDVI on BOTH dates) as the denominator. Valid/invalid grid coverage percentages use totalPixels (width × height) as the denominator.

warnings: Synthetic dataset: pixel arrays represent deterministic simulated reflectance values, not actual satellite sensor imagery.
After slice (2026-08-10) contained 2 pixel(s) where (NIR + Red) = 0; those pixels were excluded as invalid.
79 pixel(s) (13.72% of total grid) were excluded from comparison due to validity masks or zero NDVI denominators.
limitations: Detected changes represent pixel-level spectral index (NDVI) differences between the two temporal acquisitions and do NOT automatically prove real-world events such as deforestation, construction, agriculture, or hazard damage.
Optical bands (Red, NIR) are sensitive to unmasked thin clouds, cloud shadows, haze, and aerosol variations.
Solar elevation, viewing geometry, and bidirectional reflectance distribution (BRDF) illumination differences can shift index values without actual land-cover transformation.
Phenological and seasonal cycles (e.g., dry vs. wet season crop senescence) produce strong NDVI variations that require domain verification.
Sub-pixel co-registration or image alignment errors along sharp boundaries (roads, water edges, forest margins) can induce false edge-change components.

Results depend directly on the user-configured |ΔNDVI| threshold and minimum connected-component size filter; changes occurring without altering red/NIR contrast (e.g., grading bare soil to concrete of similar reflectance) may be missed.
